# Purpose

Make **one small, realistic commitment** about how you will use (and talk about) AI in your own unit, project, or role – in a way that is **secure, safe, and sustainable**.

This activity assumes we already know that tools like **Microsoft Copilot** and **Turnitin Clarity** exist, and that there may have been a **heavier ethics/policy discussion** earlier (e.g., in an Assessment 2030 session). Here, we focus on **practical next steps**, not re-stating all the risks.

---

# Option A – Full Micro-Task (10–15 minutes)

Use this version if the group still has energy to work directly with AI.

## Step 1 – Choose ONE micro-task

Pick whichever feels most useful for your context **right now**:

1. Draft a short **"AI use in this unit/team" guideline**  
2. Run a quick **risk/benefit check** on one planned AI use  
3. Draft a short **Week 1 statement** you can say to students/staff about AI

You can do this by hand or with AI support.

## Option 1 – Unit / Team AI Use Guideline

Prompt template:

> You are advising educators / professional staff at an Australian university on safe use of generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot).  
>  
> Draft a short **"AI use in this unit / team"** guideline.  
> Include:  
> - 3–4 **"Do"** points (good use cases)  
> - 3–4 **"Don't"** points (e.g., student data, confidential documents, unacknowledged AI use)  
> - A one-sentence reminder to check institutional policy.  
> Keep it under **200 words** and use plain language.

Edit the output so it:

- Fits your **tone** and context  
- Aligns with your **school/faculty policy**  
- Expresses your own view of AI as a **tool**, not a replacement

## Option 2 – Risk / Benefit Check for One Planned AI Use

Prompt template:

> You are an AI risk advisor.  
> I plan to use AI in this way in my work:  
> `[describe intended use, e.g., "Use Copilot to draft weekly announcements and example feedback comments"]`.  
>  
> Identify:  
> - Key benefits for my workload and for students/staff  
> - Main risks (privacy, bias, over-reliance, academic integrity, misinformation)  
> - 3 practical safeguards I should put in place to manage these risks in line with typical Australian university policies.

Decide which benefits and safeguards **actually apply** in your context, and note any actions you want to take.

## Option 3 – Week 1 Statement for Students or Staff

Prompt template:

> You are helping me frame AI use in my **[unit / team / project]** in a way that supports **"human irreplaceability"** (e.g., Assessment 2030).  
>  
> Suggest **3 short statements** I can say in Week 1 that:  
> - Acknowledge that AI tools exist and can be helpful  
> - Emphasise that people's unique value is in their judgement, experience, and context  
> - Encourage **transparent, responsible use**, not hidden or over-reliant use.  
> Keep each statement under **40 words** and use friendly, clear language.

Choose one you like as a starting point, and rewrite it in **your own voice**.

---

# Option B – Light Version (5–7 minutes)

Use this version if there has already been a **heavy ethics / policy session** and energy is low. No AI use required.

## Step 1 – Draft ONE clear sentence

On your own, write **one sentence** you could say in Week 1 about AI use in your context. For example:

- For students in a unit you teach  
- For research students in your group  
- For staff you support in a professional service

Your sentence should:

- Acknowledge that AI tools exist  
- Emphasise that **human judgement / learning** still matters  
- Indicate what is **allowed / expected** in your context

Examples to adapt:

- "You are welcome to use AI tools to brainstorm and draft ideas in this unit, but you are responsible for checking accuracy and making the final decisions."
- "AI can help with first drafts and summaries, but your unique value is in your judgement, experience, and ability to improve on those drafts."
- "If you use AI for your work, be transparent: tell me what you used it for and what you changed."

## Step 2 – Share (optional)

If there is time and appetite, share your sentence with your table or the whole room. Notice the different ways people balance **openness, trust, and integrity** in how they talk about AI.

---

# Variants for Researchers and Professional Staff

You can adapt Options A or B to your specific role.

## If you are mainly doing research

Possible micro-tasks:

- Draft a short **"AI in this project"** statement for an ethics application or methods section.  
- Run a risk/benefit check on using AI to:  
  - analyse transcripts  
  - summarise articles  
  - draft sections of a paper.  
- Write a Week 1 message for **HDR students** about when and how AI may be used (and documented) in their work.

## If you are in a professional / administrative role

Possible micro-tasks:

- Draft a **team-level guideline**: what your office will and will not use AI for (e.g., drafting comms vs handling student records).  
- Run a quick risk check on using AI to summarise internal documents or write student information pages.  
- Write a sentence for **staff orientation** or **student-facing materials** that sets expectations about AI use in your area.

---

# Reflection / Notes

Use the prompts below and the space provided.

- What small commitment did you make or draft in this activity (guideline, safeguard, or statement)?  
- How does it reflect a **balanced view** of AI (neither banning nor blind adoption)?  
- What is one follow-up action you could take in the next month (e.g., add this to a unit outline, syllabus, team charter, or induction slide)?
